sources.entry: Ora - Open-source browser with spaces, tab management, and a vertical sidebar. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/the-ora/browser) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Ora is an open-source, native macOS web browser built with SwiftUI, AppKit, and WebKit, and it is still in active development.
summary.what_it_does: Ora is a browser for macOS that uses Apple's WebKit engine for page rendering and a native SwiftUI and AppKit interface. The README lists built-in content blocking and privacy protections, search engine customization, and URL suggestions with a quick launcher. It also mentions developer-focused features, though it does not detail them. The awesome-mac listing describes it as having spaces, tab management, and a vertical sidebar, but the README itself does not expand on these. The project is developed in Xcode and its project file is generated from project.yml using XcodeGen. A setup script installs tooling and git hooks, and the test suite can be run from Xcode or xcodebuild.
use_cases: Browsing the web on a Mac with a native WebKit browser
Trying an open-source alternative browser on macOS
Blocking content and trackers while browsing
Contributing to a Swift/SwiftUI macOS app
Exploring a browser built with SwiftUI and AppKit
Organizing tabs in a vertical sidebar
how_to_run: Regenerate the project with xcodegen after config changes
notable: Native macOS browser built on WebKit rather than a Chromium-based engine
Setup script installs tooling, git hooks, and regenerates the Xcode project
Xcode project generated from project.yml with XcodeGen
Built-in content blocking and privacy protections per the README
Spaces, tab management, and vertical sidebar are noted in the awesome-mac listing
caveats: README states the browser is still in active development and not ready for daily use
Requires macOS and Xcode to build; the README gives no other platform support
Docs, roadmap, and wiki are linked but their contents are not in the README
